You design robot end-effectors in simulation, one part at a time. You do not write geometry: you choose a generator and its parameters (a recipe). Every recipe is built by code, checked by validators and then tested in a rigid-body physics simulator with the same wrist, timing, part, placements and scorer as every other effector. Physics decides what works; your job is to propose designs that are likely to lift and hold this part, to learn from the measured outcomes of earlier designs, and to keep each new design genuinely different from the ones already tested.

Answer only by calling submit_morphologies. Keep the analysis under 120 words and each hypothesis under 40 words. Use generic engineering language; never name a product, a company or a commercial model.

# Task

Pick the part up from a table with a top-down wrist (it moves in x, y and z and turns about the vertical axis; it cannot tilt), lift it at least 10 cm and hold it for 2 s, all within 12 s.
- Sequence, the same for every effector: settle 0.3 s; descend from above in 1 s until the effector's lowest point is at grip_height_frac x part height (at least 3 mm); close on a 1 s ramp plus 0.3 s; lift 15 cm in 1.5 s; hold.
- Held (the main score): lifted and held with no physics flag: the effector pressing the table harder than 5 N, the effector sinking more than 1 mm into the part, the part pushed away while closing, or a simulation fault.
- Registered: held, at least two effector bodies squeezing the part from directions at least 90 deg apart, and the part in the same pose as in this design's own centred grasp: within 0.75 mm, 2 deg of yaw (modulo the part's symmetry) and 3 deg of tilt.
- Tests: the screen grasps the part at 4 placements (c0 centred; c1 2 mm off centre along x; c2 3 mm off along -x; c3 1 mm off and turned 6 deg) with 2 jitter seeds each (8 episodes); the controller always aims at the centre and never knows the error. Each episode also jitters the part by up to 0.5 mm and 1 deg and the friction by 10 %.

# The parts

Every design is tested on all 6 parts below with one recipe (the same effector, the same grip_height_frac and yaw_deg on every part). A design must pass the validators on at least 4 of them; on the others it is not built and scores nothing. The goal is one effector that holds as many of these parts as possible.

## pipe_tee

- pipe_tee (pipe_tee): 1/2-inch style slip tee lying flat, branch socket toward the left jaw (+y).
- Size 60 x 44.2 x 28.5 mm (x, y, z; z up, resting on the table in this pose), mass 39.9 g (weight 0.39 N), material pvc white, yaw symmetry none.
- Features: socket branch socket (radius 10.8 mm, depth 16.5 mm, opening toward (0, 1, 0), mouth at height 14.2 mm); socket run socket pos (radius 10.8 mm, depth 16.5 mm, opening toward (1, 0, 0), mouth at height 14.2 mm); socket run socket neg (radius 10.8 mm, depth 16.5 mm, opening toward (-1, 0, 0), mouth at height 14.2 mm).
- Opening needed: in the open pose a digit pointing in direction d (deg around the vertical axis, 0 = +x, 90 = +y) must have its innermost point at least this far from the centre (mm; the outline within +-7 deg plus 5 mm): 0: 37.5, 15: 35.7, 30: 35.1, 45: 32.6, 60: 31.3, 75: 30.9, 90: 28.7, 105: 30.9, 120: 31.3, 135: 32.6, 150: 35.1, 165: 35.7, 180: 37.5, 195: 41.1, 210: 42.3, 225: 42.3, 240: 40.7, 255: 36.8, 270: 30.6, 285: 36.8, 300: 40.7, 315: 42.3, 330: 42.3, 345: 41.1.
- Reach: the digits must reach at least 38.5 mm - grip height below the palm (grip height = max(3, grip_height_frac x 28.5) mm), and grip_height_frac must stay at or below 0.82.

## block

- block (block): 30 x 40 x 60 mm block, sharp edges (no lead-in), 40 mm across the jaws.
- Size 30 x 40 x 60 mm (x, y, z; z up, resting on the table in this pose), mass 194.4 g (weight 1.91 N), material anodised aluminium, yaw symmetry 2-fold.
- Features: none (plain faces).
- Opening needed: in the open pose a digit pointing in direction d (deg around the vertical axis, 0 = +x, 90 = +y; the opposite direction is the same) must have its innermost point at least this far from the centre (mm; the outline within +-7 deg plus 5 mm): 0: 22.3, 15: 26.4, 30: 29, 45: 30, 60: 30, 75: 29.2, 90: 26.7, 105: 29.2, 120: 30, 135: 30, 150: 29, 165: 26.4.
- Reach: the digits must reach at least 70 mm - grip height below the palm (grip height = max(3, grip_height_frac x 60) mm), and grip_height_frac must stay at or below 0.92.

## hex_standoff

- hex_standoff (hex_standoff): standing hex standoff, 17 mm across flats facing the jaws, tapped top hole.
- Size 19.6 x 17 x 45 mm (x, y, z; z up, resting on the table in this pose), mass 82.9 g (weight 0.81 N), material zinc plated steel, yaw symmetry 6-fold.
- Features: socket tapped hole (radius 4.2 mm, depth 12 mm, opening toward (0, 0, 1), mouth at height 45 mm).
- Opening needed: in the open pose a digit pointing in direction d (deg around the vertical axis, 0 = +x, 90 = +y; the opposite direction is the same) must have its innermost point at least this far from the centre (mm; the outline within +-7 deg plus 5 mm): 0: 14.8, 15: 14.7, 30: 14, 45: 14.7, 60: 14.8, 75: 14.7, 90: 14, 105: 14.7, 120: 14.8, 135: 14.7, 150: 14, 165: 14.7.
- Reach: the digits must reach at least 55 mm - grip height below the palm (grip height = max(3, grip_height_frac x 45) mm), and grip_height_frac must stay at or below 0.89.

## flanged_bushing

- flanged_bushing (flanged_bushing): standing flanged bushing, 20 x 30 mm body under a 36 x 5 mm flange, 12 mm bore.
- Size 36 x 36 x 35 mm (x, y, z; z up, resting on the table in this pose), mass 90.9 g (weight 0.89 N), material brass, yaw symmetry any yaw.
- Features: socket bore (radius 6 mm, depth 35 mm, opening toward (0, 0, 1), mouth at height 35 mm); flange flange (radius 18 mm, depth 5 mm, opening toward (0, 0, -1), mouth at height 30 mm).
- Opening needed: in the open pose a digit pointing in direction d (deg around the vertical axis, 0 = +x, 90 = +y; the opposite direction is the same) must have its innermost point at least this far from the centre (mm; the outline within +-7 deg plus 5 mm): 0: 23.3, 15: 23.4, 30: 23.4, 45: 23.3, 60: 23.4, 75: 23.4, 90: 23.3, 105: 23.4, 120: 23.4, 135: 23.3, 150: 23.4, 165: 23.4.
- Reach: the digits must reach at least 45 mm - grip height below the palm (grip height = max(3, grip_height_frac x 35) mm), and grip_height_frac must stay at or below 0.86.

## l_bracket

- l_bracket (l_bracket): 40 x 40 mm L-bracket, 30 mm wide, 4 mm wall, lying flat on one leg; the jaws grip the standing leg's edges.
- Size 40 x 30 x 40 mm (x, y, z; z up, resting on the table in this pose), mass 71.6 g (weight 0.7 N), material stamped steel, yaw symmetry none.
- Features: none (plain faces).
- Opening needed: in the open pose a digit pointing in direction d (deg around the vertical axis, 0 = +x, 90 = +y) must have its innermost point at least this far from the centre (mm; the outline within +-7 deg plus 5 mm): 0: 8.8, 15: 12.5, 30: 15.6, 45: 18.1, 60: 19.6, 75: 20.1, 90: 24.5, 105: 33.1, 120: 39.8, 135: 44.2, 150: 45.8, 165: 45.9, 180: 44.5, 195: 45.9, 210: 45.8, 225: 44.2, 240: 39.8, 255: 33.1, 270: 24.5, 285: 20.1, 300: 19.6, 315: 18.1, 330: 15.6, 345: 12.5.
- Reach: the digits must reach at least 50 mm - grip height below the palm (grip height = max(3, grip_height_frac x 40) mm), and grip_height_frac must stay at or below 0.88.

## steel_slug

- steel_slug (slug): standing round steel slug, 40 mm across, 50 mm tall.
- Size 40 x 40 x 50 mm (x, y, z; z up, resting on the table in this pose), mass 494.8 g (weight 4.85 N), material ground steel, yaw symmetry any yaw.
- Features: none (plain faces).
- Opening needed: in the open pose a digit pointing in direction d (deg around the vertical axis, 0 = +x, 90 = +y; the opposite direction is the same) must have its innermost point at least this far from the centre (mm; the outline within +-7 deg plus 5 mm): 0: 25.1, 15: 25.1, 30: 25.1, 45: 25.1, 60: 25.1, 75: 25.1, 90: 25.1, 105: 25.1, 120: 25.1, 135: 25.1, 150: 25.1, 165: 25.1.
- Reach: the digits must reach at least 60 mm - grip height below the palm (grip height = max(3, grip_height_frac x 50) mm), and grip_height_frac must stay at or below 0.9.

# Generators

## fingered_hand

A round palm with 2-5 fingers hanging straight down from knuckles on a circle. Each finger is a chain of 1-3 rigid phalanges with hinge joints that close it toward the centre. Fingers are evenly spaced, or one thumb faces the others. The power synergy curls every joint; the pinch synergy closes the knuckles while the last phalanx stays upright.

| parameter | range | unit | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| n_fingers | 2-5 | count | Number of fingers on the palm. |
| n_phalanges | 1-3 | count | Links (and joints) per finger, from the knuckle to the tip. |
| layout | even, opposed | - | Where the digits sit around the palm: evenly spaced, or one thumb facing all the others. |
| spread_deg | 0-150 | deg | Opposed layout with 3 or more digits: the angle spanned by the digits that face the thumb (ignored otherwise). |
| palm_radius_mm | 15-70 | mm | Radius of the circle the knuckles sit on; with the fingers hanging straight down, a finger's inner face is this minus half its thickness and the pad. |
| palm_thickness_mm | 4-30 | mm | Thickness of the palm plate under the wrist flange; the knuckles hang from its underside. |
| finger_length_mm | 30-150 | mm | Length of one finger from the knuckle to the tip (all phalanges). |
| proximal_frac | 0.3-0.8 | - | Share of the finger length in the first phalanx; the rest is split evenly between the others (ignored with 1 phalanx). |
| finger_width_mm | 6-30 | mm | Finger width across its closing plane (the contact patch width). |
| finger_thickness_mm | 3-16 | mm | Finger thickness along the closing direction. |
| pad | none, flat, round | - | Contact pad on the inner face of every phalanx: none, a flat block, or a round bump across the finger. |
| pad_thickness_mm | 1-8 | mm | How far the pad stands out from the finger's inner face (ignored without a pad). |
| actuation | per_joint, tendon | - | per_joint: one position servo per joint; tendon: one servo per finger pulling a tendon over all its joints, so the outer phalanges keep closing after the first one is stopped. |
| grasp | power, pinch | - | power: every joint curls to wrap the part; pinch: the knuckles close while the last phalanx stays upright (per_joint) or follows passively on a spring (tendon). |
| material | pla, aluminium, steel | - | Structural material: printed PLA, machined aluminium (2.2x PLA's mass) or steel (6.3x); it sets mass and inertia, never friction. |
| grip_force_n | 5-50 | N | Total closing force shared by the digits at their nominal contact point (budget: 50 N in total and 1.5 N m per joint). |
| grip_height_frac | 0-0.9 | - | Height of the effector's lowest point above the table at the grasp, as a fraction of the part's height (never below 3 mm). |
| yaw_deg | 0-180 | deg | Rotation of the whole effector about the vertical axis relative to the part (0 puts digit 1 on the part's +y side). |

## hook_gripper

A round palm with 2-4 rigid fingers, each with a flat pad on its inner face and an inward hook lip at its tip that can catch under a rim or a flange. Fingers either swing in about a knuckle hinge or slide straight in toward the centre and stay upright, like a chuck.

| parameter | range | unit | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| n_fingers | 2-4 | count | Number of rigid fingers. |
| layout | even, opposed | - | Where the digits sit around the palm: evenly spaced, or one thumb facing all the others. |
| spread_deg | 0-150 | deg | Opposed layout with 3 or more digits: the angle spanned by the digits that face the thumb (ignored otherwise). |
| motion | swing, slide | - | swing: each finger hinges at its knuckle and swings in; slide: each finger slides straight in toward the centre and stays upright (a chuck). |
| palm_radius_mm | 15-70 | mm | Radius of the circle the finger roots sit on in the open pose. |
| palm_thickness_mm | 4-30 | mm | Thickness of the palm plate under the wrist flange; the knuckles hang from its underside. |
| finger_length_mm | 20-150 | mm | Length of a finger from its root to the underside of its hook. |
| finger_width_mm | 6-30 | mm | Finger width across its closing plane. |
| finger_thickness_mm | 3-16 | mm | Finger thickness along the closing direction. |
| pad_thickness_mm | 1-8 | mm | How far the flat pad above the hook stands out from the finger's inner face. |
| hook_depth_mm | 0-10 | mm | How far the hook lip at the fingertip reaches in beyond the pad (0: no hook, a plain padded finger). |
| hook_height_mm | 2-10 | mm | Vertical thickness of the hook lip (ignored without a hook). |
| material | pla, aluminium, steel | - | Structural material: printed PLA, machined aluminium (2.2x PLA's mass) or steel (6.3x); it sets mass and inertia, never friction. |
| grip_force_n | 5-50 | N | Total closing force shared by the digits at their nominal contact point (budget: 50 N in total and 1.5 N m per joint). |
| grip_height_frac | 0-0.9 | - | Height of the effector's lowest point above the table at the grasp, as a fraction of the part's height (never below 3 mm). |
| yaw_deg | 0-180 | deg | Rotation of the whole effector about the vertical axis relative to the part (0 puts digit 1 on the part's +y side). |

## segmented_tentacle

A round palm with 1-4 tapered digits of 3-8 rigid capsule segments. One tendon per digit curls every segment toward the centre; graded joint springs decide which end curls first, so a digit wraps around the part. A single digit can wrap a part on its own.

| parameter | range | unit | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| n_digits | 1-4 | count | Number of curling digits. |
| n_segments | 3-8 | count | Rigid capsule segments per digit, one joint each. |
| layout | even, opposed | - | Where the digits sit around the palm: evenly spaced, or one thumb facing all the others. |
| spread_deg | 0-150 | deg | Opposed layout with 3 or more digits: the angle spanned by the digits that face the thumb (ignored otherwise). |
| palm_radius_mm | 10-70 | mm | Radius of the circle the digit roots sit on. |
| palm_thickness_mm | 4-30 | mm | Thickness of the palm plate under the wrist flange; the knuckles hang from its underside. |
| digit_length_mm | 40-160 | mm | Length of one digit from its root to its tip. |
| root_radius_mm | 3-12 | mm | Radius of the segments at the root of a digit. |
| taper | 0.3-1 | - | Tip segment radius as a fraction of the root radius (linear in between). |
| curl_bias | 0-1 | - | Which end curls first under the tendon: 0 the root segments, 1 the tip segments (the joint springs are graded along the digit). |
| material | pla, aluminium, steel | - | Structural material: printed PLA, machined aluminium (2.2x PLA's mass) or steel (6.3x); it sets mass and inertia, never friction. |
| grip_force_n | 5-50 | N | Total closing force shared by the digits at their nominal contact point (budget: 50 N in total and 1.5 N m per joint). |
| grip_height_frac | 0-0.9 | - | Height of the effector's lowest point above the table at the grasp, as a fraction of the part's height (never below 3 mm). |
| yaw_deg | 0-180 | deg | Rotation of the whole effector about the vertical axis relative to the part (0 puts digit 1 on the part's +y side). |

# Rules the validators enforce

A design that breaks any rule is refused before it is simulated, with the reason.

- Bounds: every parameter of the generator, inside its range or one of its choices, nothing else.
- Build: minimum feature pla 2 mm, aluminium 1 mm, steel 1 mm; a phalanx at most pla 15, aluminium 25, steel 30 times as long as it is thick, at least 8 mm long and at least as long as it is thick; a round pad at most half its phalanx's length and half the finger's width; a hook lip at least (pad + hook depth) / 2.5 thick and no taller than half the finger; tentacle segments at least twice the minimum feature across and at least the root radius + 2 mm long.
- Open pose: digit footprints may not overlap on the palm (a digit's footprint runs from its innermost point, pad and hook included, to its back face, across its width). Digit directions: even layout 90 + 360 i / n deg (i = 0, 1, ...); opposed layout: the thumb at -90 deg and the others spread over spread_deg centred on 90 deg; yaw_deg is added to all of them.
- Mass at most 1.5 kg. At most 12 servos (per_joint: one per joint; tendon, tentacles: one per digit; hook gripper: one per finger). Closing force: each digit gets grip_force_n / digits at its contact lever (0.75 x finger length for hands, 0.85 for hook grippers, 0.6 for tentacles); that torque may not exceed 1.5 N m, and the total is at most 50 N.
- Opening: open, every digit's innermost point (palm_radius_mm minus half the finger thickness, the pad and the hook; tentacles: palm_radius_mm minus the root radius) must be at least the part's 'Opening needed' value for that digit's direction: the outline's reach within +-7 deg of the direction plus 3.5 mm of placement error and 1.5 mm. The validators use the exact direction, so between two listed directions take the larger value.
- Reach: the lowest point goes to max(3 mm, grip_height_frac x part height); the digits must reach that far below the palm with the palm's underside at least 10 mm above the part's top (finger_length_mm >= part height - grip height + 10 mm), and the lowest point must be at least 5 mm below the part's top.
- Closing: posed over the centred part and closed along its synergy, at least two effector bodies must touch the part, no two digits may run into each other before both reach it, and the digits that reach it must include two at least 90 deg apart.

# Engineering notes

These are facts about this simulation, not rules.

- Grip is friction only. The part's friction coefficient (0.3) governs every contact, so pads, materials and shapes never add grip; they decide where and how the effector touches. The squeeze each part needs (weight / friction): pipe_tee 1.3 N, block 6.4 N, hex_standoff 2.7 N, flanged_bushing 3 N, l_bracket 2.3 N, steel_slug 16.2 N; the digits must squeeze at least that in total to lift it, and about twice that to survive the 1 g shake test.
- Each digit closes with grip_force_n / digits at its nominal contact point and stops when it meets the part. A digit that meets nothing stops at its joint limit with no force.
- Swinging digits rotate about their knuckle, so they meet a vertical face at an angle and their tips rise as they close; sliding digits move straight in and stay upright. A power grasp curls every joint; a pinch keeps the last phalanx upright.
- Digits converge as they close. Neighbours that are close in angle or wide can run into each other before they reach a small part.
- A hook only helps where something overhangs, such as a flange or a rim; on a plain face it behaves like a narrower pad.
- Every effector body is gravity compensated (the arm carries the effector), so mass only adds inertia; the 1.5 kg limit still applies.
- The wrist cannot tilt. Placement errors are unknown to the controller: the open effector must clear the part wherever it actually is, and registration then asks the grasp to bring the part back to the same pose every time.

# Designs already tested

- t1 fingered_hand [nemotron]: held 0/48, registered 0/48; failures: invalid_build 16, missed_grasp 16, slip_during_lift 16; per part (held, registered): pipe_tee 0 %/0 %, block 0 %/0 %, hex_standoff 0 %/0 %, flanged_bushing 0 %/0 %, l_bracket 0 %/0 %, steel_slug 0 %/0 %
  params {"actuation":"tendon","finger_length_mm":85,"finger_thickness_mm":6,"finger_width_mm":14,"grasp":"pinch","grip_force_n":14,"grip_height_frac":0.55,"layout":"opposed","material":"aluminium","n_fingers":3,"n_phalanges":2,"pad":"flat","pad_thickness_mm":3,"palm_radius_mm":40,"palm_thickness_mm":12,"proximal_frac":0.5,"spread_deg":100,"yaw_deg":15}
  idea: Three-finger tendon pinch with wider spread and larger palm gives adequate opening for irregular parts while keeping joint count low.
- t2 fingered_hand [nemotron]: held 24/48, registered 15/48; failures: invalid_build 16, not_registered 9, slip_during_lift 8; per part (held, registered): pipe_tee 0 %/0 %, block 100 %/50 %, hex_standoff 100 %/62 %, flanged_bushing 100 %/75 %, l_bracket 0 %/0 %, steel_slug 0 %/0 %
  params {"actuation":"per_joint","finger_length_mm":95,"finger_thickness_mm":5,"finger_width_mm":12,"grasp":"power","grip_force_n":18,"grip_height_frac":0.6,"layout":"even","material":"steel","n_fingers":4,"n_phalanges":1,"pad":"round","pad_thickness_mm":2,"palm_radius_mm":38,"palm_thickness_mm":10,"proximal_frac":0.5,"spread_deg":60,"yaw_deg":45}
  idea: Four-finger even power grasp with longer fingers provides high force and redundancy for bulky components while respecting servo limits via reduced phalanges.

# Diversity rule

Distances are in points: within one generator each number's range is 100 points and a different choice counts 100 points; designs of different generators are always far apart. Unused parameters (spread_deg of an even layout or of a two-digit design, proximal_frac with one phalanx, pad_thickness_mm without a pad, hook_height_mm without a hook) are reset to their defaults and numbers are rounded to 0.5 mm, 1 deg, 0.5 N or 0.01 before comparing. Every new design must be at least 100 points from every tested design and from the other new designs, or it is refused as too similar; an identical one is refused as a duplicate.

# What to submit

Call submit_morphologies once. Write the analysis first: what the measured outcomes and the geometry tell you, and your plan. Then give exactly 4 designs in "designs". For each design give a hypothesis (what it should do and why), the generator name in "kind", and in "params" every parameter of that generator (a number inside its range, or one of its choices), even the ones the design does not use.

# Some designs were refused

Your previous call was:

These designs were refused and were not simulated:

- design 1: buildable on 3 of 6 parts (needs 4); pipe_tee: too_narrow: open, digit 3 (at -126 deg on the part) has its inner face 39.0 mm from the centre; the part reaches 36.6 mm that way, so it needs 41.6 mm (3.5 mm placement error + 1.5 mm clearance; palm_radius_mm sets it); hex_standoff: digit_collision: closing over hex_standoff, digits 1 and 2 run into each other at 18 % closure before both reach the part (spread them, narrow them or grip a wider section); l_bracket: too_narrow: open, digit 2 (at 162 deg on the part) has its inner face 39.0 mm from the centre; the part reaches 40.9 mm that way, so it needs 45.9 mm (3.5 mm placement error + 1.5 mm clearance; palm_radius_mm sets it)
- design 4: buildable on 2 of 6 parts (needs 4); pipe_tee: too_narrow: open, digit 1 (at -75 deg on the part) has its inner face 24.0 mm from the centre; the part reaches 31.8 mm that way, so it needs 36.8 mm (3.5 mm placement error + 1.5 mm clearance; palm_radius_mm sets it); block: too_narrow: open, digit 1 (at -75 deg on the part) has its inner face 24.0 mm from the centre; the part reaches 24.2 mm that way, so it needs 29.2 mm (3.5 mm placement error + 1.5 mm clearance; palm_radius_mm sets it); l_bracket: too_narrow: open, digit 2 (at 105 deg on the part) has its inner face 24.0 mm from the centre; the part reaches 28.1 mm that way, so it needs 33.1 mm (3.5 mm placement error + 1.5 mm clearance; palm_radius_mm sets it); steel_slug: too_narrow: open, digit 1 (at -75 deg on the part) has its inner face 24.0 mm from the centre; the part reaches 20.1 mm that way, so it needs 25.1 mm (3.5 mm placement error + 1.5 mm clearance; palm_radius_mm sets it)

Call submit_morphologies again with exactly 4 designs. Keep design 2, design 3 exactly as they were. Replace each refused design with a new one that fixes the stated problem and still follows every rule and the diversity rule.
